sourceFindings.finding: NetworkSetting::Bandwidth uses fewer rounds and more bytes; cryptographic checks remain enabled.
The network setting chooses Normal versus Reduced PRF implementation, not insecure mode.
TLS connection driver starts the handshake independently and admits application writes only after handshake completion. This supports holding an open fresh session before a request.

constraints: Known jobs and their challenges existed before preparation; not an unknown-job session pool.
TLS connection was opened before the trigger; the HTTP request was submitted only after it.
TLS warming used a three-second driver hold followed by a two-second demonstration hold; readiness was not proven by a public handshake-ready API.
Each query used a fresh single-use session; no session key or MPC material reuse.
Local historical timer excluded final JSON parsing and JavaScript live job validation, although those checks subsequently passed.
Loopback results do not include full peer job delivery, witness selection or independent operators.
Existing authenticated TLS session-time freshness rules remain unchanged and can reject sessions opened before an unknown job window.
Normal MPC, certificate verification, pinned notary key and authenticated job challenge remained enabled; no Proxy-TLS or full reveal shortcut.
Fewer rounds trade increased communication for latency; traffic below one megabyte has not been achieved.
Two samples per configuration do not establish tail latency, a network SLA or formal security equivalence.
No benchmark artifacts, runtime secrets, local user paths or private keys are published in this evidence file.
